scope: B-cell lymphomas (mature B-cell neoplasms). Built from WHO-HAEM5 (2022) and ICC (2022); both are in simultaneous use and disagree on several entities. Internal research substrate only; NCCN not used.
schema_note: Classification axis is entity + lineage/grade + defining genetics, NOT histologic-pattern-as-primary. Each record carries who5 and icc fields because the two 2022 systems diverge — this divergence is the freshness-critical axis for lymphoma articles.

classification_records.divergence: Concordant as an entity, but cell-of-origin handling differs in emphasis; ICC retains MYC/BCL6 double-hit cases here or in HGBL-NOS.
classification_records.morphology: Diffuse proliferation of large transformed B-cells (centroblastic, immunoblastic, or anaplastic variants) effacing nodal architecture.
classification_records.cell_of_origin: Hans algorithm (CD10, BCL6, MUM1/IRF4) divides into GCB vs non-GCB; gene-expression profiling divides GCB vs ABC vs unclassified.
molecular_signature: heterogeneous; LymphGen-type genetic subtypes (MCD, BN2, N1, EZB, etc.) emerging in research/clinical use
classification_records.grading_system: Not graded; COO subclassification is the key stratifier
classification_records.clinical_note: Most common aggressive B-cell lymphoma. COO and double-hit status carry prognostic and increasingly therapeutic weight.

classification_records.entity: DLBCL/HGBL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (double-hit, BCL2)
classification_records.icc_term: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements
classification_records.divergence: MATERIAL: WHO5 calls it DLBCL/HGBL-MYC/BCL2 (morphology-agnostic once FISH known); ICC prefers 'high-grade B-cell lymphoma'. BOTH now restrict the category to MYC+BCL2 — MYC/BCL6-only double-hit cases were removed and reassigned to DLBCL-NOS or HGBL-NOS.
classification_records.morphology: Large-cell, intermediate, or blastoid morphology; morphology no longer defines the category once dual rearrangement is confirmed.
classification_records.cell_of_origin: Germinal-center / dark-zone biology; GCB by Hans.
ihc_signature: MYC and BCL2 protein co-expression common but NOT equivalent to rearrangement
molecular_signature: MYC rearrangement AND BCL2 rearrangement by FISH (± BCL6)
classification_records.clinical_note: FISH for MYC, BCL2, BCL6 is required to identify this group. Double-hit (MYC/BCL2) carries adverse prognosis and influences regimen intensity. This is the single highest-yield WHO5/ICC distinction to get right.

classification_records.divergence: Concordant; receives MYC/BCL6 double-hit cases that no longer qualify for the MYC/BCL2 category, plus blastoid/intermediate cases lacking double-hit genetics.
classification_records.morphology: Blastoid or intermediate-sized cells between DLBCL and Burkitt, without defining double-hit MYC/BCL2 genetics.
molecular_signature: lacks the MYC+BCL2 dual rearrangement defining the DH category; MYC/BCL6 cases land here
classification_records.clinical_note: A heterogeneous NOS bucket; the MYC/BCL6-rearranged cases reassigned here lack a unifying biology.

classification_records.divergence: Renamed from 'Burkitt-like lymphoma with 11q aberration' (WHO-HAEM4R) because molecular profiling shows it is closer to DLBCL than to Burkitt.
classification_records.morphology: Starry-sky pattern resembling Burkitt; may have coarser nuclei/greater pleomorphism.
molecular_signature: 11q centromeric gains with telomeric losses (11q24qter); LACKS MYC rearrangement (distinguishes from Burkitt)
classification_records.clinical_note: MYC-negative, 11q-defined; the absence of MYC rearrangement is the key separator from Burkitt.

classification_records.morphology: Medium-sized monomorphic cells, squared-off cytoplasm, starry-sky from tingible-body macrophages, near-100% proliferation.
molecular_signature: MYC rearrangement (t(8;14) or variants) as sole primary hit; lacks BCL2 rearrangement
classification_records.clinical_note: MYC-driven without BCL2 translocation; distinction from HGBL/DLBCL with double-hit hinges on this and on BCL2 status.

classification_records.entity: Primary large B-cell lymphoma of immune-privileged sites
classification_records.who5_term: Primary LBCL of immune-privileged sites (CNS, vitreoretinal, testis)
classification_records.icc_term: Handled as separate primary entities (e.g., PCNSL) — divergence in grouping
classification_records.divergence: WHO5 conceptually MERGED immune-privileged-site LBCLs (CNS, testis, vitreoretinal) into one family; ICC keeps them more separate. A clear grouping divergence.
classification_records.morphology: DLBCL morphology in CNS, testis, or vitreoretinal compartment.
molecular_signature: MYD88 L265P and CD79B mutations frequent
classification_records.clinical_note: Shared immune-privileged biology and MYD88/CD79B genetics underpin the WHO5 merger.

classification_records.divergence: Concordant; gray-zone lymphoma (mediastinal, between PMBL and classic Hodgkin) recognized by both.
classification_records.morphology: Sheets of large clear cells with compartmentalizing sclerosis in anterior mediastinum.
classification_records.cell_of_origin: Thymic B-cell origin; distinct from DLBCL-NOS.
classification_records.clinical_note: Young adults; PD-L1 biology makes checkpoint blockade relevant. Distinguish from gray-zone lymphoma.

classification_records.divergence: MATERIAL: WHO5 de-emphasizes the 1-2-3A numeric grading and introduces a biology-based framework (classic FL, follicular large B-cell lymphoma, and distinct subtypes); ICC retains more of the traditional grading. Reconcile carefully.
classification_records.morphology: Follicular (± diffuse) proliferation of centrocytes and centroblasts recapitulating germinal centers.
ihc_signature: BCL2+ (in neoplastic follicles — key vs reactive)
classification_records.grading_system: WHO5: classic FL vs FL with predominantly diffuse pattern vs follicular large-B-cell; ICC: grades 1-3A vs 3B
classification_records.clinical_note: Most common indolent B-cell lymphoma. BCL2 positivity within follicles separates neoplastic from reactive hyperplasia. Grade 3B behaves aggressively.

classification_records.entity: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL)
classification_records.divergence: Largely concordant; monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis thresholds and progression handled similarly.
classification_records.morphology: Small mature lymphocytes with proliferation centers (pseudofollicles); SLL is the tissue-based, non-leukemic counterpart.
classification_records.grading_system: Not graded; prognosis by IGHV status, TP53/del(17p), and cytogenetics
classification_records.clinical_note: CD5+/CD23+/cyclin D1- phenotype and LEF1 distinguish from mantle cell. TP53/del(17p) and IGHV status drive therapy selection.

classification_records.who5_term: Mantle cell lymphoma (with in-situ mantle cell neoplasia, leukemic non-nodal, and classic/blastoid recognized)
classification_records.divergence: Concordant; both recognize leukemic non-nodal MCL and in-situ mantle-cell neoplasia as distinct from classic nodal MCL.
classification_records.morphology: Monomorphic small-to-medium cells with irregular nuclei; classic, blastoid, and pleomorphic variants.
classification_records.cell_of_origin: Naive/pre-GC B-cell (SOX11+); leukemic non-nodal often SOX11-negative, IGHV-mutated.
molecular_signature: rare cyclin D1-negative cases use SOX11/CCND2-3 rearrangement
classification_records.grading_system: Ki-67 proliferation index is the key prognostic grade; blastoid/pleomorphic adverse
classification_records.clinical_note: Cyclin D1 + t(11;14) define it; SOX11 helps in cyclin D1-negative cases. Ki-67 index and TP53 drive risk. Distinguish from CD5+ CLL by cyclin D1/SOX11+ and CD23-.

classification_records.entity: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of MALT (MALT lymphoma)
classification_records.who5_term: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue
classification_records.icc_term: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of MALT
classification_records.divergence: Concordant. Nodal and splenic marginal zone lymphomas are separate entities in both.
classification_records.morphology: Marginal-zone (centrocyte-like) cells, lymphoepithelial lesions, reactive follicles colonized by tumor.
molecular_signature: t(11;18) API2::MALT1 (gastric, predicts H. pylori-eradication resistance)
classification_records.clinical_note: Antigen-driven (e.g., H. pylori in gastric MALT); t(11;18) predicts failure of antibiotic therapy. Diagnosis of exclusion among small B-cell lymphomas — needs full IHC panel to exclude CLL/MCL/FL.

classification_records.divergence: Concordant; MYD88 L265P central to both.
classification_records.morphology: Spectrum of small B-cells, plasmacytoid lymphocytes, and plasma cells; Dutcher bodies; mast cells.
classification_records.cell_of_origin: Post-GC B-cell differentiating toward plasma cell.
classification_records.clinical_note: MYD88 L265P supports the diagnosis and is therapeutically relevant (BTK-inhibitor sensitivity); CXCR4 status modifies response. WM = LPL with IgM paraprotein + marrow involvement.

classification_records.entity: Large B-cell lymphoma arising in immune deficiency/dysregulation
classification_records.who5_term: LBCL associated with immune deficiency/dysregulation (unified framework)
classification_records.icc_term: Classified within a different organizing scheme for immunodeficiency-associated LPDs
classification_records.divergence: MATERIAL: WHO5 created a unified immune deficiency/dysregulation framework with a standardized three-part naming (clinical setting + pathology + virus); ICC organizes these differently. A structural divergence worth an article of its own.
classification_records.morphology: Polymorphic to monomorphic LBCL, often EBV-driven, in post-transplant/iatrogenic/inborn-error/HIV settings.
molecular_signature: fewer driver mutations than sporadic DLBCL in some settings
classification_records.clinical_note: The WHO5 unified naming is the freshness-critical point; reducing immunosuppression is often first-line in PTLD-type disease.

high_yield_divergences: Double-hit category now MYC+BCL2 only (both systems); MYC/BCL6 reassigned to NOS.
WHO5 'DLBCL/HGBL-MYC/BCL2' vs ICC 'HGBL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements' terminology.
Follicular lymphoma grading: WHO5 biology-based reframing vs ICC traditional grades.
Immune-privileged-site LBCLs merged in WHO5; separate in ICC.
Immune deficiency/dysregulation: WHO5 unified three-part naming vs ICC scheme.
Burkitt-like with 11q renamed to HGBL/LBCL with 11q aberration (MYC-negative).
notes: Every aggressive-LBCL article MUST state which classification it follows and flag where WHO5 and ICC diverge. This is the lymphoma analogue of the breast WHO5-reclassification trap. Verify entity names against current WHO-HAEM5 and ICC at write time.
